newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge expected to rule shortly on Liggett.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge expected to rule shortly on Liggett.

text.p: The judge overseeing Florida's lawsuit against U.S. cigarette makers on Monday heard arguments on releasing secret Liggett Group documents but made no immediate ruling.

Lawyers for both the state of Florida and the tobacco companies said Palm Beach County Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen was likely to rule this week. The losing side was likely to appeal Cohen's decision, the lawyers said.

Stephen Krigbaum, an attorney for Philip Morris Cos Inc, one of the defendants, said Cohen had made no ruling after hearing tobacco company lawyers argue that eight documents in dispute were covered by attorney-client privilege and contained no evidence of crimes.

Attorneys pressing Florida's claim of $1.0 billion or more for money spent by the state to treat sick smokers have argued the papers contain damning evidence of conspiracy by tobacco companies to hide the dangers of smoking.

Florida's attorneys want to use the papers at a trial scheduled for August 4. The documents are among those turned over last month to anti-tobacco lawyers by Liggett Group, a unit of Brooke Group, as part of a settlement with state attorneys general.
The eight papers are largely notes from meetings among tobacco company lawyers planning defenses against lawsuits in past decades, Krigbaum said.

On Monday, Cohen was considering the recommendation of William Rutter, an outside lawyer he appointed to review the secret documents. Rutter last week recommended the eight documents be released, and Cohen may endorse, reject or modify that recommendation.
